annotations.text:
VERIFIED — Open-ticket list

/Tickets and /Opportunities are the same endpoint; the difference is the `domain` filter. The default (domain=reqs) returns 3,924 open tickets; domain=all returns 4,242 — matching the DB. The 318 missing are opportunities (domain=opportunities). The add-in never passes domain, and tickettype_id / ticketarea_id / isopportunity on /Tickets are silently ignored.

For the biggest clients 85–90% of what IS returned is project sub-tasks (DaVinci: 98 of 116 are 'Project User To-Dos'; CIT: 51 of 75). 2,509 of 3,924 sit in 'Task - Waiting User'; 2,779 are Unassigned. The list renders them flat, unsorted, with 5 interactive pills per row.

VERIFIED — Client resolution

When the sender isn't already an exact-email contact, the fallback is /Client?search=<email domain>. That returns 0 for a real customer (cpnllc.com → Central Point Networks) because client search matches names, and the AREA.ADomain / aAzureDomain fields are populated on 0 of 496 active clients. Result: no client → no ticket list → agent sees 'None'.

findUserByEmail also takes the first fuzzy hit when there's no exact match — 'freitas' returns a service account first.

VERIFIED — Append picker

/Tickets?search= returns closed tickets (4 of 5 'printer' hits are closed), matches on body text, and does not return statusname — so the '· status' suffix the picker tries to show is always blank. client_name IS returned but never shown.

search=#9517 → 0 results; search=9517 → the ticket. The compose pane looks up staged tickets as '#<id>', so the 'Will append to…' banner never gets its summary.

Cap is 15 mixed rows, no scope, no open/closed distinction.

VERIFIED — What actually lands in Halo

The 4 add-in-logged actions in the DB (signature: AMailEntryID set; none of the last 30 native rows have it) all stored EmailDirection = '', emailto = '', emailcc = '', emailbodyhtml = NULL. Only noteHTML survived. Native intake rows store full To/Cc lists.

Caveat: those rows came from the previous production build; the payload now sends direction/to/body but no add-in email has been logged since Sep 3, so whether Halo persists the new fields is still unproven. The note body is the one channel proven to survive — hence the envelope block.

Office.js gives the read pane To/Cc synchronously (item.to / item.cc) and the full .eml via getAsFileAsync (Mailbox 1.14; the task pane manifest floor is 1.10, so feature-detect).

CODE-VERIFIED — Compose pane

Six stacked sections behind dividers; 'Log on send' — the reason the pane exists — is fifth, below three insert tools and a native <select>. The timer takes a full section. The staged-ticket banner is what the agent needs to see before hitting Send, so it moves to the top.
